1) Laws that are abolished: laws kept as a model are abolished when the reality comes.

1. The holy laws of sacrifice (chapters 1~10)
 1) The five great offerings of Leviticus (chapters 1~7): burnt offering, grain offering, peace offering, sin offering, guilt offering
 ① Burnt offering: to burn, to roast. A sacrifice in place of the sinner who would burn in the fire of hell. It means devotion.
 ② Grain offering: it's a gift. Offering a gift of fine flour to God. Grinding the wheat and burning it.
가루가 되어야 하나가 된다.\n ③ 화목제 : 속죄만 하고 끝나는 것이:
You have to become flour to become one.
 ③ Peace offering: it doesn't end with just atonement; you must go on to reconciliation. In the peace offering the one who offered it can share in eating it too. An offering of sharing
 - In the case of a bull, after taking out the priest's share, there's about 600 kg (1,000 geun) of meat, and it all has to be eaten within a day or two. You can't do a peace offering by inviting only people close to you; it's only possible if you invite everyone
 ④ Sin offering: only sins committed unknowingly are forgiven
 - Sins committed on purpose, intentionally, with planning, repeatedly, continually, it says the person must be put to death.
 ⑤ Guilt offering: when you've caused loss to God or to a neighbor or brother, you must repay it with 20% added.
The law of setting apart as holy – the first thing it deals with is the offerings: no human sacrifice.
두 번 반복 되는데 앞부분은 제사 드리는 사람이 제물을 어떻게 드릴 것인: It's repeated twice, and the first part is about how the person offering the sacrifice should present the offering.
The second part is about how the priests should conduct the sacrifices.

3. Priorities in the life of faith seen through the structure of Leviticus
 1) Chapters 1~10: a life of worship, our relationship with God, is the most important
